FileFolderInfo — Windows 10 x64 test package

IMPORTANT: this is a test build, not a release. The context-menu DLL starts the separate Ultralight helper process for the built-in map option; WebCore is never loaded inside Explorer. Keep the complete extracted folder structure together, especially FileFolderInfo.dll and the sibling map-probe folder.

1. Extract the whole archive to a normal local folder. Do not run files from inside the ZIP.
2. To install the Explorer context-menu extension, right-click install.bat and choose Run as administrator. The DLL registers its CLSID and ContextMenuHandlers entries in HKLM. The script asks before restarting Explorer; choose Y to refresh the menu now, or N and restart Explorer manually later.
3. To remove the registration, run uninstall.bat as administrator. Keep FileFolderInfo.dll beside the script until unregistration completes. The script also asks before restarting Explorer.
4. In file metadata, each GPS map row now has an Open... button. It offers (1) the built-in Ultralight window, which must load the selected service URL, (2) the Windows default browser, or (3) a detected installed browser. Detection checks Windows browser registrations and common App Paths entries; it does not change the default browser. The built-in viewer opens at map-probe/FileFolderInfoMap.exe.
5. The standalone probe is still available: open map-probe and run run_probe.bat. It displays the Leaflet test map and requests OpenStreetMap tiles over the network. Use run_probe_noanim.bat for the comparison run with Leaflet zoom animation disabled. Logs are written beside the executable.
6. Test on the intended Windows 10 x64 virtual machine. Check registration/menu visibility; for every GPS service test the built-in URL, the default browser, and at least one browser in the "Open in another" submenu. Also test tiles, wheel zoom, and resizing in the standalone probe. Attach map-probe/ultralight_probe_input.log and map-probe/ultralight_probe.log if present.

Troubleshooting: if registration reports that a module cannot be found, check that the Windows image has the system DLLs imported by FileFolderInfo.dll (including msi.dll). If the built-in viewer reports that its helper is missing, re-extract the complete archive and do not move the DLL away from map-probe. Do not copy Windows system DLLs from this archive or another machine into the system folders. The built-in web engine's compatibility with each mapping site remains to be confirmed on the target VM; this test does not claim compatibility with a clean Windows installation or other architectures.
